findings.title: OpenAI sk-proj-* key format not redacted
findings.description: The OpenAI pattern \bsk-[A-Za-z0-9]{40,80}\b requires 40+ consecutive alphanum chars immediately after sk-. OpenAIs current key format (since mid-2024) is sk-proj-<48_alphanum>, which contains a hyphen after sk- that is not in [A-Za-z0-9]. The regex matches at most 4 chars (proj) before stopping at the second hyphen, failing the 40-char minimum. A real sk-proj- key in a Bash command, Edit payload, or tool response will be logged unredacted.
findings.attack_path: The unguarded path is a bare string value: e.g. {"api_key": "sk-proj-XXXXXXXX"} in tool_input JSON. Dict keys are intentionally not walked, and the api[_-]?key case-insensitive pattern covers api_key= in key=value form but not when the JSON dict key is api_key. A raw sk-proj- string not adjacent to a recognized keyword lands in the log unredacted.
findings.remediation: Extend the OpenAI pattern to cover sk-proj- prefix: re.compile(r"\bsk-(?:proj-[A-Za-z0-9_\-]{40,90}|[A-Za-z0-9]{40,80})\b"). Add a test case sk-proj-AAAA...AA (48 chars) to tests/test-redaction.sh.

findings.title: Shell init files .bash_profile / .profile / .zprofile / .zshenv absent from Edit and Write deny rules
findings.description: The 5e35b4f expansion covers ~/.bashrc and ~/.zshrc but omits other shell init files sourced by login shells: ~/.bash_profile, ~/.bash_login, ~/.profile, ~/.zprofile, ~/.zshenv. On macOS the default login shell is zsh; ~/.zprofile is sourced before ~/.zshrc. An agent blocked from editing ~/.zshrc can write a persistent payload to ~/.zprofile instead.
findings.attack_path: Claude attempts Edit(~/.zshrc) -> blocked. Attempts Edit(~/.zprofile) -> passes deny rules, passes safety-warn.sh (pattern covers .env, .pem, .key, id_rsa, credentials files -- not shell profiles). Edit succeeds, adding a command that runs on next terminal open.
findings.remediation: Add Edit(~/.zprofile), Edit(~/.zshenv), Edit(~/.bash_profile), Edit(~/.bash_login), Edit(~/.profile) to the deny list, with corresponding Write entries.

findings.title: Log files created 0o644 (world-readable) while ~/.claude/ directory is 755
findings.description: atomic_append creates log files with mode 0o644. The ~/.claude/ directory is drwxr-xr-x (755) -- confirmed by directory listing. Any local user can read ~/.claude/logs/tool-calls-*.jsonl. Redaction is the only protection; given known gaps (sk-proj-*, DATABASE_URL non-URL values, dict keys not walked), residual unredacted data can persist world-readable. Impact is low on single-user macOS but meaningful on shared developer machines or CI runners.
findings.attack_path: A second local user reads ~/.claude/logs/tool-calls-YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl and finds an unredacted sk-proj- key that appeared in a Bash tool call.
findings.remediation: Change atomic_append to create files with mode 0o600. Harden install_logs_dir in scripts/install.sh: mkdir -p "${CLAUDE_DIR}/logs" && chmod 700 "${CLAUDE_DIR}/logs".

findings.title: DATABASE_URL / CONNECTION_URL not in SCREAMING_SNAKE suffix list
findings.description: The P1-4 fix covers URL userinfo passwords embedded in connection strings via the URL userinfo pattern. However, DATABASE_URL as a variable name with a non-URL value (e.g. DATABASE_URL=prod-db-hostname) is not redacted: URL is absent from the SCREAMING_SNAKE suffix list (PASSWORD|PASSWD|SECRET|TOKEN|KEY|PAT|CREDENTIAL|CREDENTIALS|AUTH), and the generic case-insensitive pattern does not include url as a keyword.
findings.attack_path: A Bash tool call runs echo DATABASE_URL=$DATABASE_URL for debugging. The value is a non-URL DSN or hostname and is logged as-is even though it may identify a sensitive production resource.
findings.remediation: Add DATABASE_URL and CONNECTION_URL to the SCREAMING_SNAKE alternation (or add the URL suffix broadly). Add a test case DATABASE_URL=prod-hostname-sensitive to tests/test-redaction.sh.

findings.title: ~/.bashrc and ~/.zshrc absent from Read deny -- asymmetry with Edit/Write deny
findings.description: Every credential-store path in the Edit/Write deny lists also appears in Read deny -- except ~/.bashrc and ~/.zshrc. Shell rc files commonly contain exported secrets. Claude reading these files exposes those secrets to the logging pipeline and to the Stop hook fast model (issue #5). The asymmetry appears unintentional.
findings.attack_path: Claude reads ~/.zshrc to help debug a shell issue. The file contains export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-xxx. The value appears in a PostToolUse log entry; if log is world-readable (SEC-3), any local user can extract it.
findings.remediation: Add Read(~/.bashrc) and Read(~/.zshrc) to the deny list, matching the Edit and Write entries for these two files.

residual_risks.description: Dict keys in tool_input JSON are intentionally not walked by redact_value (_log_core.py line 110). Claude Code tool schemas do not put secrets in key names, but a malicious or malformed MCP server could. Accepted design trade-off.
The Authorization/Bearer pattern will false-positive on legitimate non-credential strings (e.g. Bearer realm in WWW-Authenticate headers). Log-fidelity risk, not a security risk.

Issue #2 (bash -c bypass) and issue #5 (Stop hook transmits unredacted response to fast model) remain the highest-severity residual security risks. Tracked as open GitHub issues, excluded per audit instructions.
Third-party LLM provider key formats not covered: Replicate (r8_...), Hugging Face (hf_...). Out of scope for current pattern set.

testing_gaps.description: No test case for OpenAI sk-proj-* format in tests/test-redaction.sh. The existing sk- test uses the legacy 40+ alphanum format; the sk-proj- format requires a separate case.
test-settings-valid.sh checks deny rule count >=30 but does not assert that specific high-risk paths (e.g. shell profile files) are present in the deny list.
test-hooks.sh verifies log file creation but does not assert the mode of the created file (should be 0o600 after SEC-3 remediation).
